title: Diagnose and repair local Ruff and Mypy failures the way CI runs them
narrative: Fangore's PR checks keep dying on Ruff import order and Mypy untyped defs before pytest even matters. He starts guided coding against a temp workspace that already has a CI-shaped failure log and a broken module, asks the local Completer to read the static-check output (or re-run the same tool), repair the file, and leave a short fix note. Host `verify_runs` re-check with `ruff: true` / `mypy: true` so the story proves the cheap Completer lane can clear the same static gates CI uses. Complements `fangore_coding_ci_diagnose` (forge log lookup) and `fangore_coding_ci_repair` (seeded runtime/pytest repair).
implementation: Agentic Recipe catalog id `guided_coding` with `environment.local_work: project_coding`, `static_seed: ruff_imports|mypy_untyped`, and `coding_tool_script: static_ruff_repair|static_mypy_repair`. Seeds plant `messy.py` / `typed_mod.py` plus `.mechaharness/ci_failure.log`. `ProjectCodingLocalWork` `verify_runs` accepts `ruff` and `mypy` rows (``python -m ruff check`` / ``python -m mypy``). Soft point `external_guidance` remains the human scope gate.
validation: Harness `user_story` scenarios `ruff.yaml` and `mypy.yaml` in suite `fangore_guided_coding`. Static mode uses the named coding_tool_scripts. Asserts the repaired module and `.mechaharness/ci_fix.md` cite Ruff I001 or Mypy no-untyped-def, and start inputs include matching `verify_runs`. Live Completer may drive the same tools with `MECHA_STORY_BACKEND=live`.
